text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: SLO breach detected for shared-gpu-pool-3. p99 latency for streaming API spiked to 18s, p95 at 4.2s over last 5m. Affected tenants: tenant-psi, tenant-pulse. Auto-mitigation not triggered (thresholds set at p99>10s). Please ack and triage.
Aisha: Ack. I'm on it. gathering quick metrics now.
kevin: I'm reachable if you need help, will pull pool-level IO and cgroup stats.
Aisha: Stack: serving-runtime v2.3, kernels gpu-allocator v1.0, running multi-tenant q4 configs. Symptoms: streaming stalls (clients report partial frames, long gaps). Not a full outage but SLO breach for several customers.
Aisha: Running `curl` to poll metrics endpoint...
Aisha: ```
GET /metrics?pool=shared-gpu-pool-3
--
streaming.kafka.latency.p99 18.2
serving.runtime.tokens/sec 45
gpu0.io.read_latency_ms 12.1
cgroup.io.writeback.ms 240
``` 
kevin: nvidia-smi shows limited GPU memory pressure but high PCIe write stalls on node gpu-node-17. grabbing `iostat` and `bpftrace` traces.
kevin: ```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device:   rrqm/s wrqm/s  r/s  w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s  avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await  r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1  0.00  12.00  0.00 40.00 0.00   3200.00   80.00    4.21     35.0  0.00   35.0    1.20   48.0
```
kevin: Looks like high write throughput causing IO queuing on GPU nodes; may be noisy tenant doing periodic large checkpoints.
Aisha: Checking tenant processes: `ps -ef | grep tenant-pulse` shows they hit heavy snapshot writes at ~10s intervals.
Sasha: pinging infra team to see if any background backups or host-level jobs overlapped.
infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance job `backup-window-3` started 2026-03-15T02:10Z on gpu-node-17. Owner: infra-scheduled. (automated note)
Aisha: That explains the writepressure. backup + tenant checkpointing = cgroup IO saturation. I'm going to temporarily lower tenant-pulse IO share and move tenant-psi to another pool.
kevin: How fast can we evict and migrate? We have live connections but streaming supports session migration with short reconnects.
Aisha: Migration plan: 1) Reduce tenant-pulse blkio weight to 40 using `cgset`. 2) Create new ephemeral pool gpu-pool-burst (on nodes 21-22) and migrate tenant-psi there. 3) If writeback remains high, throttle backups (ask infra).
ops-lead: Approve throttling backups if customer impact reduces. Notify infra-runbook owner now.
Aisha: Executing step 1:
Aisha: ```bash
cgset -r blkio.weight=40 /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-pulse
``` 
Aisha: Done. Observing immediate drop in write queues on node-17. p99 down to ~12s but still elevated.
kevin: Initiating migration for tenant-psi to gpu-pool-burst. Kicking off drain on their pods with `kubectl rollout restart --namespace tenant-psi` and `evict` with graceful 15s.
kevin: ```
kubectl cordon node gpu-node-17
kubectl drain node gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=15
``` 
Aisha: Customer-ops: can you notify tenant-psi and tenant-pulse about potential brief reconnects? Keep message minimal.
customer-ops: Messaging draft: "We're investigating higher-than-normal latency on streaming endpoints. You may experience a brief reconnect while we migrate traffic; no data loss expected. We'll post updates in 15m." Approving send now.
customer-ops: Sent to primary contacts for both tenants.
Sasha: Any metrics on percent of traffic from noisy tenant? If it's small but heavy IO, we can isolate without broad disruption.
kevin: tenant-pulse accounts for ~22% of streaming tokens on this pool but ~65% of write IO during checkpoints (from iostat correlation)
Aisha: After cgset and initial eviction, p95 now 1.1s, p99 6.2s. Still above SLO but much improved.
Aisha: Starting full migrate of tenant-psi to gpu-pool-burst. ETA ~2m.
kevin: Migration completed. Pods scheduled on nodes 21-22. Confirming traffic shift in envoy metrics.
Aisha: envoy: active_conns for tenant-psi dropped on pool-3 and rose on gpu-pool-burst. Good.
Aisha: p99 now 2.4s, p95 0.9s. Streaming stalls no longer reproduced in logs. Will keep monitoring for 20m.
Sasha: Great. Next steps: 1) Keep blkio limit for tenant-pulse for next 24h. 2) Re-run tenant checkpoint cadence suggestions with SE to reduce overlap with infra backups. 3) Ask infra to reschedule backup-window-3.
ops-lead: I'll open a follow-up ticket to coordinate tenant checkpoint cadence and backup windows. Assign to infra and customer-eng.
Aisha: Filing incident timeline and mitigation steps into postmortem doc now. Will include graphs and raw `iostat`/`nvidia-smi` snippets.
incidents-bot: Incident severity escalated to P2 for tracking; pages cleared for on-call.
kevin: One more datapoint: found one host-level cron on gpu-node-17 `/usr/local/bin/metrics-archiver` that ran concurrently with backup-window-3. Recommend removing cron or throttling it.
infra-bot: Cron owner tagged: infra-ops-team. Created ticket INF-4821 to reschedule.
customer-ops: Customers acknowledged message and appreciate quick mitigation. No immediate complaints.
Sasha: Handoff to night oncall @Sasha in 10m. I'll track until then and drop an exec summary.
Aisha: Exec summary: root cause - concurrent infra backup + tenant checkpoint causing cgroup blkio saturation and PCIe write stalls; impact - p99 streaming latency spike to 18s, affected tenants tenant-psi (migrated) and tenant-pulse (IO-limited); mitigation - reduced blkio weight for tenant-pulse, migrated tenant-psi to isolated pool, scheduled infra ticket to move backup, crons adjusted; current state - p99 stabilized ~2.4s, p95 ~0.9s, monitoring for 20m.
Sasha: Thanks. I'll continue watch and follow up on the INF ticket and postmortem. Good triage team. :thumbsup:
Aisha: Leaving a final note in the thread and closing my oncall handoff. last-check p99 2.3s, p95 0.8s.
Sasha: Acknowledged handoff. If anything regresses please @Sasha and I'll wake the oncall
